memory_candidates.content: In BimodalLogic, a frame built by FrameOver.ofReflectiveRegular must never be unfolded inside simp/rw to reach its TaskRel; cite the frame's own named bridge lemma instead (e.g. RefinedFilteredTaskFrame.rel_iff). Reason: TaskFrame.Limit is a semireducible def and TaskFrame.limit_of_permissive/limit_of_succOrder/limit_of_shift are declared with the UNFOLDED return shape, so the auto-generated _proof_4 of such a frame carries an unfolded type while the constructor expects TaskFrame.Limit R. Any tactic match that re-typechecks the constructor application under reducible/implicit transparency then fails with 'pattern not found' plus an application type mismatch naming _proof_4 -- a misleading diagnostic that looks like cited-lemma drift and is not fixed by substituting a differently-named taskRel lemma. The sibling proofs (_proof_2 Compositional, _proof_3 Serial, _proof_5 Saturation) are folded and fine, which makes the asymmetry easy to miss. Term-mode application at default transparency sidesteps the whole class. The convention is documented in TaskFrame.lean's ofReflective_taskRel docstring; it affects every ofReflectiveRegular frame whose hlim comes from those helpers (RegionFrame, FlowFrame, ForwardDeterministicFrame, LimitClosureFrame and others).
